paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU Pro confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy metrics. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, with a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, and tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.01 to 0.02. The y-axis represents Accuracy, with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, and tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Final Accuracy, shown in blue with circle markers and a solid line style, Δ Accuracy, shown in orange with diamond markers and a dashed line style, and Initial Accuracy, shown in green with square markers and a dotted line style. The blue line starts at approximately 0.95 at an initial confidence of 0.81 and ends at around 0.99 at an initial confidence of 0.99, remaining relatively stable with minor fluctuations. The orange line starts at approximately 0.4 at an initial confidence of 0.81 and ends at around 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.99, generally decreasing with some fluctuations. The green line starts at approximately 0.6 at an initial confidence of 0.81 and ends at around 0.8 at an initial confidence of 0.99, showing an overall increasing trend with some fluctuations.
